We need to propose retrosynthesis route with 3 reactions for target SMILES: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2)cc1

We need to produce JSON route with 3 reaction steps (retro). Steps correspond to forward hints: 1) carboxylic acid to amide (coupling). 2) Doebner modification (aldehyde + malonic acid -> α,β-unsaturated acid). 3) sulfonamide formation (amine + sulfonyl chloride). So retrosynthetic direction: target -> break amide bond to give acid and amine; break α,β-unsaturated acid to aldehyde + malonic acid? Actually Doebner modification forward: aldehyde + malonic acid -> α,β-unsaturated acid. So retro: break the C=C and C=O to give aldehyde and malonic acid? The product is unsaturated amide? Wait target has /C=C/C(=O)N... So the unsaturated acid is part of amide after coupling. So retro steps: Step1: disconnect amide between C(=O) and N of aniline (Nc3ccccc3N). So precursors: unsaturated acid (C=C-COOH) attached to phenyl sulfonyl? Actually the unsaturated acid is attached to phenyl sulfonyl? Let's parse target: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2)cc1

We have a tolyl (methyl phenyl) attached to sulfonamide linking to another phenyl ring (c2ccc(... )cc2) which has a side chain /C=C/C(=O)N-aryl-NH2 (an aniline). So overall: tolyl-sulfonamide-phenyl-CH=CH-CO-NH-phenyl-NH2? Actually Nc3ccccc3N is an aniline with NH2 para? It's an aniline (aniline with NH2). So the amide is between carbonyl and aniline nitrogen (attached to phenyl). So step1: amide formation from unsaturated acid (C=C-COOH) and aniline (c3ccccc3N). So retro: target -> unsaturated acid + aniline.

Step2: unsaturated acid derived from Doebner modification: aldehyde (maybe p-? The aldehyde is attached to phenyl ring (c2ccc(... )cc2). So the aldehyde is on that phenyl ring: c2ccc(CHO)cc2? Actually the side chain is attached to phenyl via /C=C/. The unsaturated acid is attached to phenyl via double bond. So the aldehyde precursor is aromatic aldehyde attached to phenyl (c2ccc(CHO)cc2). So retro: unsaturated acid -> aromatic aldehyde + malonic acid (or malonic acid derivative). So we need aldehyde (c2ccc(CHO)cc2) and malonic acid (HOOC-CH2-COOH). The Doebner modification forms α,β-unsaturated acid (c2ccc(/C=C/COOH)cc2). So step2: break that to aldehyde + malonic acid.

Step3: sulfonamide formation: target has sulfonamide linking to tolyl (methyl phenyl) and phenyl sulfonyl chloride? Actually sulfonamide formed from amine (tolyl amine?) The sulfonamide is NS(=O)(=O) attached to phenyl ring (c1ccc...). The sulfonamide nitrogen is attached to tolyl ring (the N is attached to tolyl? Actually Cc1ccc(N S(=O)(=O) c2ccc(... )cc2)cc1. So the sulfonamide nitrogen is attached to tolyl ring (an aniline). So sulfonamide formed from tolyl amine (p-toluidine) and sulfonyl chloride derived from phenyl sulfonyl chloride (c2ccc(SO2Cl)cc2). So retro: break sulfonamide to tolyl amine and phenyl sulfonyl chloride.

Thus three steps: 1) amide formation (coupling) between unsaturated acid and aniline (c3ccccc3N). 2) Doebner modification: aldehyde + malonic acid -> unsaturated acid. 3) sulfonamide formation: tolyl amine + phenyl sulfonyl chloride -> sulfonamide.

Now we need to find template IDs for each transformation. Use search_template_catalog_by_criteria for each.

First, amide formation: functional_groups_broken: aliphatic carboxylic acid? Actually forward: carboxylic acid + amine -> amide, breaking C-O bond of acid (carboxylic acid) and forming C-N. So broken functional group: aliphatic carboxylic acid (since unsaturated acid is aliphatic). Formed: amide. Use search.
